_README: Copy this file to credentials.json (same directory) and fill in real values. credentials.json is git-ignored and must NEVER be committed. Every key can also be supplied as an environment variable instead — see algos/shared/credentials.py for the exact names.
_telegram_token: From @BotFather: /newbot, then copy the HTTP API token. Env: LWG_TELEGRAM_TOKEN
_telegram_chat_id: The GROUP the bots broadcast to (negative number, e.g. -1001234567890). Add the bot to the group, send a message, then read chat.id from https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates. Env: LWG_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
_deadman_url: The EXTERNAL dead-man's switch ping URL, e.g. https://hc-ping.com/<uuid> from a free healthchecks.io check. algos/notifications/deadman.py pings it every 5 minutes ONLY while the bots are healthy, so the ABSENCE of a ping is what alerts you - the one failure no on-box alert can report, because a dead VPS cannot tell you it died. Treat it as a SECRET: anyone holding it can send your pings for you and keep the alert permanently green. Leave empty to run without one (supported - the script says so and exits 0). Env: LWG_DEADMAN_URL
_github_token: A GitHub FINE-GRAINED personal access token, so the VPS can commit and push the bot's decision record ITSELF instead of waiting for a Mac to wake up. Scope it to ONE repository with Contents: Read and write and nothing else - Metadata: Read-only is forced by GitHub and is not a choice. Set a long expiry or none: a token that lapses stops the backup silently, which is the failure mode this whole job exists to avoid. It is read at run time and spliced into the push URL in memory, so it never reaches .git/config where a config dump or a screenshot would show it. Env: LWG_GITHUB_TOKEN. Leave empty and the box does not push - the Mac-side sync still works, which is the arrangement this replaced. WHY IT IS HERE AT ALL: the VPS scheduled task runs as SYSTEM, whose credential store has no cached token and no interactive session to ask for one, so git push BLOCKS rather than failing (measured 2026-08-05). WHAT IT COSTS: this box already holds a live broker password, and a token beside it means a break-in costs you the repository too - the one-repo scope is the whole of the limit on that.
_telegram_health_chat: A SEPARATE group for algos/notifications/log_review.py's findings (negative number). This traffic is routine chatter about the bots' own health, and the day you mute it you must not also mute the group carrying your fills — which is why it is its own chat. Getting the id: create the group, add the bot, then send a SLASH COMMAND in it (/status) — the bot's BotFather privacy mode is ON, so it never receives a plain group message and getUpdates stays empty; stop the Telegram bot first (schtasks /change /tn SYS_TELEGRAM /disable, then kill it) or its long-poll consumes the update before you can read it. Leave empty and findings go to telegram_chat_id, and the tool SAYS which it used. Env: LWG_TELEGRAM_HEALTH_CHAT
_telegram_signal_chat: A SEPARATE group for PRE-TRADE SETUP alerts (negative number) - a setup forming, its entry zone going live, a rule blocking it, and what became of it. Aaron's is "LWG Capital Signals". Its own room because it is a third reflex, read when you have time rather than the moment it arrives, and because it is MEASURED at ~10x the volume of fills (20.2 messages/month against 2, one every 1.5 days, on sos_fade over 6.5 years) - putting that in the trades group would bury the fills. Getting the id is the same trick as telegram_health_chat above and has the same two traps, BOTH of which look like an empty getUpdates: (1) BotFather privacy mode is ON so the bot never receives a plain group message - send a SLASH COMMAND (/status); (2) the running Telegram bot long-polls with an offset that DELETES each update, and SYS_MONITOR restarts it within ~60s, so disable the task first (schtasks /change /tn SYS_TELEGRAM /disable), kill it by scoped commandline, send /status, read chat.id from getUpdates WITHOUT an offset parameter, then re-enable and schtasks /run. RE-ENABLE IT - while that task is disabled nothing on the box sends a fill alert and nothing reports that it is off. Easiest alternative: open the group in web.telegram.org and read the number out of the URL. Leave empty and setup alerts fall back to telegram_chat_id and say so once. Env: LWG_TELEGRAM_SIGNAL_CHAT
_telegram_admin_chat_id: Your PERSONAL chat id (positive number) for critical alerts. Same getUpdates trick, from a direct message to the bot. Env: LWG_TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID
_mt5_accounts: Per-account MT5 logins, keyed by account number as a STRING: {"12345678": {"password": "...", "server": "VantageMarkets-Demo"}}. A live bot names its account in its own instance config and the password is looked up here, so the two never travel together and one credentials file serves every bot on the machine.
_per_bot_telegram: A bot can report to its OWN group, as its OWN Telegram identity, without any change to this file's shape. The destination is a plain chat id in the bot's instance config (telegram_chat_id). A separate identity is a key added HERE and NAMED there (telegram_token_key), e.g. "telegram_token_bleg": "<token from a second BotFather bot>" — env: LWG_TELEGRAM_TOKEN_BLEG. Any key works; the env name is always LWG_<KEY IN CAPS>. Leave both empty on a bot and it uses the shared token and group above.
